title: TUI wizard: create a roadmap interactively
lead:
Add a guided "wizard" to the ncurses UI that walks a user through building a roadmap
from scratch — slicer prompting for each field it needs, then landing the items (and
their slices) directly.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Today the only ways into a roadmap are `slicer add` (one item, title only, then `promote`
plus one `edit` per section) or hand-writing an outline for `slicer import`. Both assume
the user already knows slicer's field model and the outline grammar. A wizard prompts for
what slicer needs and lands the items for you, lowering the barrier for a fresh project.
The user chose in-curses step-by-step prompts over an `$EDITOR`-backed skeleton.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
`src/slicer/tui.py` (new wizard mode + entry points); a new in-terminal text-input
primitive (in `tui.py` or a small new module) since the TUI has none — every edit today
suspends curses and hands off to `$EDITOR` via `_via_editor`; `tests/test_tui.py`. Reuse
`outline.ItemSpec`/`SectionSpec` and `ops.apply_outline` rather than inventing a new apply
path.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
The wizard collects answers into `ItemSpec`s that apply to the same result as the
equivalent `import`. Cancelling writes nothing (all-or-nothing, like `apply_outline`). The
text-input primitive (echo, backspace, Enter to accept, Esc to cancel) is exercised as a
pure function, matching the module's "thin drawing loop, pure functions above it"
discipline.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. A reusable in-terminal text-input primitive (the core new capability), with its
   decidable logic pure and testable and only the raw key loop touching curses.
2. A wizard flow: optional project/document title, then a per-item loop — title, size,
   tree(s), findings, importance, urgency, group, depends — then offer the configured
   `sections` to fill, then "add another item?".
3. Collect answers into `outline.ItemSpec` objects and apply via `ops.apply_outline`
   (all-or-nothing; allocates ids; resolves `depends`-by-title; validates) — the exact path
   `import` uses, so the wizard inherits its guarantees.
4. Entry points: a `w` key, and offer the wizard automatically when the roadmap is empty
   (the loop already special-cases the empty roadmap).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
unittest suite green; from an installed build, launch the TUI on an empty project, run the
wizard, and confirm items and slices land and `slicer check` is green.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit.

**Not in this slice:** rich in-curses text editing (multi-line section bodies may still
hand off to `$EDITOR`); editing existing items via the wizard (the TUI already edits
fields and sections in place); mouse support and multi-column forms. Whether to also
persist the collected answers as a durable outline `.md` is decided during implementation;
re-import/round-trip of any such file is out of scope. This slice is large — the
text-input primitive is a natural split point and may become its own prerequisite slice.
